notes: Step 1 parts were correct, so I kept them unchanged.
The circuit image is the authority on connections. Signal path: Vidor D2 -> green wire -> column 3 -> 82 ohm resistor -> column 6 -> LED anode. LED cathode (column 8) -> black wire -> Vidor GND.

The catalogue calls the half of the breadboard holding rows f-j bank 'b'. The image's upper half is labelled j-f, so I used 'b' ids: green wire at 3b.g, resistor legs at 3b.h and 6b.h, LED legs at 6b.i and 8b.i, black wire at 8b.h.
The LED's bent, longer leg (anode) is in column 6, next to the resistor. The straight leg (cathode) is in column 8 and goes to GND. This puts the resistor on the anode side, as drawn.
The pin labelled '2' on the image is D2 on the catalogue card. The sketch's ledPin = 2 agrees.
The 82 ohm resistor limits the current at the Vidor's 3.3 V logic level. Each physical join has both a joined and an electrical edge.
The USB cable for power and programming is implied but not drawn, so it is not in the graph.
